title: Arise, Shine — It Is Your Season to Shine
excerpt: A Sunday Service message from Isaiah 60:1 calling believers to arise from sin, fear, discouragement, shame, bitterness and unforgiveness, receive God’s healing, and manifest His glory.
tags: Manifestation of the Glory of God
content:
“Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.” — Isaiah 60:1

It Is a Season to Shine

The message opened with a repeated declaration from Isaiah 60:1: Arise. Shine. The Lord has commanded His people not to remain in the same state forever. There comes a moment when God calls His sons and daughters out of shame, insecurity, fear and everything that has kept them hidden.

“My daughter, my son, you have stayed there for long. It is your time to arise.”

We arise because our light has come, and we shine so that the glory of God may be manifested through our lives. The call to arise is therefore not merely encouragement. It is a command that demands a response.

There Is an Urgency to Arise

The preacher emphasized the urgency contained in the word arise. When something is urgent, we do not remain passive; we take the necessary step.

“The Lord has called me and commanded me to arise and shine. What is the necessary step that I am taking?”

For one person, that step may be repentance. For another, it may be confronting fear, seeking healing, releasing bitterness, forgiving, resting, or choosing to continue after discouragement. The question is personal: what is keeping you from arising?

Do Not Make Pain Your Permanent Dwelling Place

The message identified fear, hatred, bitterness, sin and unresolved pain as things that can hold a person down. Pain is real, but it must not become the place where we permanently live.

“You cannot arise if you keep making the place of pain your permanent dwelling place.”

The response is not to pretend that the wound never happened. It is to bring it before God: “Lord, heal me. Lord, help me. Heal my heart. Heal my soul.” Healing prepares us to arise.

Hindrance One: Sin — Take the Step of Repentance

Isaiah 59:2 was used to show how sin disrupts fellowship with God: “Your iniquities have separated you from your God.”

The necessary response is repentance. Confess the sin before God, turn back to Him, and make your heart right with Him. The message carried a strong assurance alongside the call to repentance: the Lord is ready to embrace you back.

Sin → separation → repentance → confession → restoration.

Hindrance Two: Fear — Elijah Must Arise Again

In 1 Kings 19:1–8, Elijah had experienced a great victory, yet Jezebel’s threat caused him to become afraid and run for his life. His fear eventually took him into the wilderness, where his discouragement became so deep that he asked God to take his life.

But God met Elijah there. An angel touched him and said, “Arise and eat, for the journey is too great for you.”

The sermon drew a practical lesson from Elijah: arising sometimes requires rest and nourishment. Elijah rested, received nourishment, regained strength, arose and continued his journey. Fear did not have to determine the end of his story.

Do not allow fear to determine the direction in which you arise.

God Still Has a Journey for You

Elijah’s story became an encouragement to anyone who feels exhausted by the journey. The Lord still has plans for His people. However difficult the journey has been, discouragement does not mean that God has finished with you.

The preacher also emphasized meeting God in the secret place: as we open ourselves to Him, He meets, restores and strengthens us.

Hindrance Three: Discouragement — Keep Building

Nehemiah 4 provided another picture of people trying to fulfil an assignment while facing mockery, threats, opposition and exhaustion. Tobiah mocked the wall they were building, and their enemies plotted to create confusion and stop the work.

Yet Scripture says, “So we built the wall … for the people had a mind to work.” They prayed to God and also set a guard.

Eventually the workers admitted that their strength was failing and that there was too much rubble. The message was clear: discouragement can stop you from moving even when God has called you. Do not abandon the assignment because the journey became difficult.

Do Not Let Your Past Define Your Future

The sermon then addressed shame and painful experiences from the past.

“Don’t let your past define your future.”

A shameful moment is not your permanent identity. What happened before must not be allowed to cancel what God intends to do through your life now. Yesterday’s pain must not become today’s prison.

Bitterness and Unforgiveness — A Message of Freedom

The message concluded its list of hindrances by addressing bitterness and unforgiveness. A wound may be genuine, but the wound should not be allowed to control the rest of your life.

“Don’t allow the wound to control your life.”

Bitterness and unforgiveness keep the heart tied to what happened. The invitation was therefore toward freedom: allow God to heal the heart, surrender the wound and refuse to make bitterness your identity.

The preacher described the movement of healing as going from wounded to strong, broken to forgiven, and bitterness to kindness.

Healing Prepares You to Arise

The central application became simple: allow God to heal you. Healing is not separate from the call to arise; it prepares you to arise.

The message moved into corporate prayer with a cry for God’s mercy: “Lord, have mercy on me.” The congregation was invited to open their hearts before God and ask Him to search what is within.

Arise and Manifest His Glory

Isaiah 60:1 remained the foundation from beginning to end. God has not called His people to remain permanently in fear, shame, sin, discouragement, bitterness or pain.

Repent where repentance is needed. Rest where you need restoration. Receive God’s healing. Forgive. Release the past. Take the necessary step. Then arise and shine.

“It is your time to arise. The Lord has commanded you: Arise and shine.”

The purpose is greater than personal recovery. We arise so that the life and glory of God can become visible through us.

Scriptures from the Message

  • Isaiah 60:1 — Arise, shine, for your light has come.
  • Isaiah 59:2 — Sin separates people from fellowship with God.
  • 1 Kings 19:1–8 — Elijah’s fear, exhaustion, restoration and renewed journey.
  • Nehemiah 4 — Continuing God’s work despite mockery, opposition and discouragement.
